title: How to Prepare for Carpet Installation: Furniture, Doors and Old Carpet
meta: Clear the small stuff, leave heavy furniture to the crew, plan for doors and old carpet removal. Wills Flooring's carpet prep checklist for Everett homes.
keywords: how to prepare for carpet installation, what to do before carpet installers come, do carpet installers move furniture, remove old carpet before installation, carpet installation checklist, doors after new carpet

blocks.lead: Empty the closets and small items, leave the heavy furniture to the crew if it is in the quote, do not pull the old carpet yourself unless you have agreed to, and expect interior doors to come off for the day.
blocks.detail: Most Everett carpet jobs are one day per floor. The prep that matters happens the week before: deciding who moves what, who removes the old carpet, and what happens to doors that will not clear the new pile. Both of those jobs are priced lines, $0.25 and $0.45 per sq ft, on top of the $0.99 per sq ft install.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks, "Installers are coming Tuesday, what do I actually need to do?" The answer depends on your quote, and Everett has every version of the job: a Silver Lake two-story emptied while a Boeing shift worker sleeps elsewhere, a Riverside 1910s home with original doors, a Port Gardner condo with an elevator to reserve. This is the carpet installation checklist we send our own customers.

blocks.text: Furniture: what to move and what to leave

items.title: You handle the small stuff
items.text: Everything on the floor that fits in a box: shoes, toys, baskets, lamps, cords, plants and the contents of closets, plus anything on a low shelf that could fall. Empty dressers of heavy contents if we are moving them.

items.title: The crew handles the big pieces, if quoted
items.text: At $0.25 per sq ft, beds, dressers, sofas and dining sets move room to room as we work, then go back at the end. Whole-house jobs need a staging plan, usually the garage or the kitchen, which is why we ask at the estimate.

items.title: What no installer moves
items.text: Pianos, gun safes, aquariums, waterbeds, pool tables and most large electronics. Those need a specialty mover before the day. A grand piano in a Bayside living room has stopped more than one install at 8 a.m.

items.title: Timing for shift workers
items.text: Everett runs on Boeing and hospital schedules. If you sleep days, tell us and we sequence rooms so the bedroom is done first or last.

blocks.text: Old carpet: pull it yourself or leave it?

a.title: Choose this when
items: You want one day of disruption instead of a weekend of your own labor
There may be pet stains, mold or an unknown subfloor underneath
The house has stairs; tack strip on stairs is sharp and awkward
You want disposal handled; a transfer station run costs time and a truck

b.title: Choose this when
items: You have asked for it and the quote drops the $0.45 per sq ft removal line
You want to see what is under the carpet before install day
You can pull every staple and the tack strip without gouging the subfloor
You can leave the subfloor swept clean, with nails and debris gone

blocks.title: If you find hardwood under the carpet:
blocks.text: Stop and call before the install date. Riverside and Bayside homes from the 1900s to 1920s often have fir or oak under the carpet. You may still want carpet, but decide with the wood in view, and the tack strip plan changes so the wood stays refinishable.

items.html: Interior doors come off. We take them down to work and rehang them at the end. If a thicker pad or taller pile makes a door drag, we tell you. Trimming a door is a carpenter's task, and hollow-core doors can only lose so much.
Baseboards stay. Carpet is tucked under the baseboard gap. Baseboards set tight to the subfloor in older Everett homes may show a small gap; caulk fixes it.
Paint first, then carpet. Paint walls and trim before install day so drips land on old carpet. Touch-ups go on after we leave. Do not schedule a painter for the same day.
Heat on, windows openable. Carpet and pad relax and stretch better at room temperature, and new carpet has a smell for a day or two that a cracked window handles.

items.text: We confirm the rooms, the carpet and pad, where furniture is going and where the van parks. In a Port Gardner condo this is when the elevator pad and quiet hours matter.

Old carpet is cut into strips, rolled and hauled with the pad. Staples and tack strip come out, the subfloor is swept and checked for squeaks and stains. Anything unexpected is shown to you before we cover it.
New tack strip around the perimeter, pad rolled, seamed and fastened. This is the loud part of the day.
Carpet is rough cut, seamed with a heat iron, then power stretched wall to wall onto the strip. Edges are tucked, doorways get transitions, doors go back on.

items.d: End of day · Furniture back and walkthrough
items.text: Furniture returns, scraps are yours if you want a piece for repairs, and we walk the rooms with you. Vacuuming right away is fine.

items: Pets. Carpet day is loud and doors are open. A closed room with a blanket, or a day at a friend's house, is kinder for everyone.
Parking. In Riverside and near downtown Everett, a spot near the door saves the crew a lot of carrying.
Closet systems bolted to the floor. They need to come out or be planned around.
Where the leftover carpet goes. Keep a doormat-sized piece for future repairs; it will match in a way a new order never will.

faq.a: Most do when it is agreed in advance. Wills Flooring lists it as a line on the written quote at $0.25 per sq ft. Beds, dressers, sofas and tables are moved room to room and put back. Pianos, safes, aquariums, waterbeds and large electronics are never moved by the crew.

faq.q: Should I remove the old carpet myself before installation?
faq.a: Only if you have asked and the quote reflects it. Tear-out and disposal run $0.45 per sq ft including haul-away, so pulling it yourself saves less than people expect and you lose the chance for us to see the subfloor first. If you do it, pull every staple and the tack strip.

faq.q: Do I need to take the doors off for carpet installation?
faq.a: No, the crew does that. Interior doors come off so the carpet can be tucked and stretched cleanly, then they are rehung. If the new pad and carpet are thicker than the old, a door may drag. We flag it before we leave; trimming a door is a carpenter's job.

faq.q: How long does carpet installation take in one day?
faq.a: A typical Everett main floor or three bedrooms is one working day, arriving around 8 and finishing mid afternoon, including tear-out. Stairs add several hours at $30 a step. Whole-house jobs with two floors and stairs run two days. Seams and stretching take the same care in any size room.

faq.q: Should I paint before or after new carpet?
faq.a: Before. Paint walls and trim ahead of install day so drips land on the old carpet, then do small touch-ups afterward. Baseboards stay in place during carpet installation, so there is no need to wait for them. Never book a painter for the same day as the flooring crew.

faq.q: Can I vacuum new carpet right away?
faq.a: Yes. Vacuuming on day one is fine and helps lift loose fibers left from cutting the edges and seams. Shedding for the first few weeks is normal on cut-pile carpet and is not a defect. Use a vacuum with an adjustable height so the beater bar does not fuzz the pile.
